source_text:
Postquam perscripseram librum hunc, venit nuntius ille, qui me tradiderat huic pastori, in domum, in qua eram, et consedit supra lectum, et adstitit ad dexteram hic pastor. Deinde vocavit me et haec mihi dixit:
Tradidi te, inquit, et domum tuam huic pastori, ut ab eo protegi possis. Ita, inquam, domine. Si vis ergo protegi, inquit, ab omni vexatione et ab omni saevitia, successum autem habere in omni opere bono atque verbo et omnem virtutem aequitatis, in mandatis huius ingredere, quae dedi tibi, et poteris dominari omni nequitiae.
Custodienti enim tibi mandata huius subiecta erit omnis cupiditas et dulcedo saeculi huius, successus vero in omni bono negotio te sequetur. Maturitatem huius et modestiam suscipe in te et dic omnibus, in magno honore esse eum et dignitate apud dominum et magnae potestatis eum praesidem esse et potentem in officio suo. Huic soli per totum orbem paenitentiae potestas tributa est. Potensne tibi videtur esse? Sed vos maturitatem huius et verecundiam, quam in vos habet, despicitis.
Dico ei: Interroga ipsum, domine, ex quo in domo mea est, an aliquid extra ordinem fecerim, ex quo eum offenderim.
Et ego, inquit, scio nihil extra ordinem fecisse te neque esse facturum. Et ideo haec loquor tecum, ut perseveres. Bene enim de te hic apud me existimavit. Tu autem ceteris haec verba dices, ut et illi, qui egerunt aut acturi sunt paenitentiam, eadem quae tu sentiant et hic apud me de his bene interpretetur et ego apud dominum.
Et ego, inquam, domine, omni homini indico magnalia domini; spero autem, quia omnes, qui antea peccaverunt, si haec audiant, libenter acturi sunt paenitentiam vitam recuperantes.
Permane ergo, inquit, in hoc ministerio et consumma illud. Quicumque autem mandata huius efficiunt, habebunt vitam, et hic apud dominum magnum honorem. Quicumque vero huius mandata non servant, fugiunt a sua vita et illum adversus; nec mandata eius sequuntur, sed morti se tradunt et unusquisque eorum reus fit sanguinis sui. Tibi autem dico, ut servias mandatis his, et remedium peccatorum habebis.
Misi autem tibi has virgines, ut habitent tecum; vidi enim eas affabiles tibi esse. Habes ergo eas adiutrices, quo magis possis huius mandata servare; non potest enim fieri, ut sine his virginibus haec mandata serventur. Video autem eas libenter esse tecum; sed ego praecipiam eis, ut omnino a domo tua non discedant.
Tu tantum communda domum tuam; in munda enim domo libenter habitabunt; mundae enim sunt atque castae et industriae et omnes habentes gratiam apud dominum. Igitur si habuerint domum tuam puram, tecum permanebunt. Sin autem pusillum aliquid inquinationis acciderit, protinus a domo tua recedent; hae enim virgines nullum omnino diligunt inquinationem.
Dico ei: Spero me, domine, placiturum eis, ita ut in domo mea libenter habitent semper. καὶ ὥσπερ οὗτος, ᾧ παρέδωκάς με, οὐ μέμφεταί με, οὐδὲ αὗται μέμψονταί με.
λέγει τῷ ποιμένι: Οἶδα, ὅτι ὁ δοῦλος τοῦ θεοῦ θέλει ζῆν καὶ τηρήσει τὰς ἐντολὰς ταύτας καὶ τὰς παρθένους ἐν καθαρότητι καταστήσει.
ταῦτα εἰπὼν τῷ ποιμένι πάλιν παρέδωκέν με καὶ τὰς παρθένους καλέσας... λέγει αὐταῖς: Quoniam video vos libenter in domo huius habitare, commendo eum vobis et domum eius, ut a domo eius non recedatis omnino. Illae vero haec verba libenter audierunt.
Ait deinde mihi: Viriliter in ministerio hoc conversare, omni homini indica magnalia domini, et habebis gratiam in hoc ministerio. Quicumque ergo in his mandatis ambulaverit, vivet et felix erit in vita sua; quicumque vero neglexerit, non vivet et erit infelix in vita sua.
Dic omnibus, ut non cessent, quicumque recte facere possunt; bona opera exercere utile est illis. Dico autem, omnem hominem de incommodis eripi oportere. Et is enim, qui eget et in cotidiana vita patitur incommoda, in magno tormento est ac necessitate.
Qui igitur huiusmodi animam eripit de necessitate, magnum gaudium sibi adquirit. Is enim, qui huiusmodi vexatur incommodo, pari tormento cruciatur atque torquet se qui in vincula est. Multi enim propter huiusmodi calamitates, cum eas sufferre non possunt, mortem sibi adducunt. Qui novit igitur calamitatem huiusmodi hominis et non eripit eum, magnum peccatum admittit et reus fit sanguinis eius.
Facite igitur opera bona, quicumque accepistis a domino, ne, dum tardatis facere, consummetur structura turris. Propter vos enim intermissum est opus aedificationis eius. Nisi festinetis igitur facere recte, consummabitur turris, et excludemini.
Postquam vero locutus est mecum, surrexit de lecto et apprehenso pastore et virginibus abiit, dicens autem mihi, remissurum se pastorem illum et virgines in domum meam.
thought_title: The angel's final charge and the virgins' guardianship
orientation: The book ends in Hermas’s own house. The angel who first handed him over to the Shepherd comes, sits on the bed, and gives him a last charge about the commandments, the virgins who are to live with him, and doing good before the tower is finished.
pass_a_gloss: After I had written this book, that messenger who had handed me over to this shepherd came into the house in which I was, and sat down on the bed, and this shepherd stood at his right hand. Then he called me and said these things to me: 'I have handed you over,' he said, 'and your house to this shepherd, so that you may be able to be protected by him.' 'Yes, Lord,' I said. 'If therefore you wish to be protected,' he said, 'from every vexation and from every cruelty, and to have success in every good work and word and every virtue of righteousness, walk in the commandments of this one, which I have given to you, and you will be able to rule over all wickedness. For if you keep the commandments of this one, every desire and sweetness of this world will be subject to you, and success in every good undertaking will follow you. Receive his maturity and modesty into yourself and tell everyone that he is in great honor and dignity with the Lord and that he is a ruler of great power and powerful in his office. To him alone over the whole world has the power of repentance been granted. Does he seem powerful to you? But you despise his maturity and the reverence that he has toward you.' I say to him: 'Ask him yourself, Lord, since he has been in my house, whether I have done anything out of order, by which I have offended him.' 'And I,' he said, 'know that you have done nothing out of order and are not going to. And therefore I speak these things with you, so that you may persevere. For this one has thought well of you here with me. But you will say these words to the rest, so that those too who have done or are going to do repentance may feel the same things as you, and this one may interpret well about them here with me, and I with the Lord.' And I said, 'Lord, I declare the great works of the Lord to every person; but I hope that all who have sinned before, if they hear these things, will willingly do repentance, recovering life.' 'Remain therefore,' he said, 'in this ministry and complete it. But whoever carries out the commandments of this one will have life, and great honor here with the Lord. But whoever does not keep the commandments of this one flees from his own life and opposes him; they do not follow his commandments, but hand themselves over to death, and each one of them becomes guilty of his own blood. But I tell you to serve these commandments, and you will have a remedy for sins. But I have sent you these virgins, so that they may dwell with you; for I saw that they are kindly disposed to you. You have them therefore as helpers, so that you may be more able to keep the commandments of this one; for it cannot happen that these commandments are kept without these virgins. But I see that they are willingly with you; but I will command them not to depart from your house at all. Only cleanse your house; for in a clean house they will dwell willingly; for they are clean and chaste and industrious and all have favor with the Lord. Therefore if they have your house pure, they will remain with you. But if any little bit of defilement happens, they will immediately withdraw from your house; for these virgins love no defilement at all.' I say to him: 'I hope, Lord, that I will please them, so that they will always dwell willingly in my house. And just as this one, to whom you handed me over, does not find fault with me, neither will these find fault with me.' He says to the shepherd: 'I know that the servant of God wishes to live and will keep these commandments and will establish the virgins in purity.' Having said these things to the shepherd, he again handed me over, and calling the virgins, he says to them: 'Since I see that you dwell willingly in this man's house, I entrust him to you and his house, so that you do not withdraw from his house at all.' But they heard these words willingly. Then he said to me: 'Conduct yourself manfully in this ministry, declare the great works of the Lord to every person, and you will have favor in this ministry. Whoever therefore walks in these commandments will live and will be happy in his life; but whoever neglects them will not live and will be unhappy in his life. Tell everyone not to cease, whoever can do rightly; to practice good works is useful for them. But I say that every person ought to be rescued from hardships. For he who is in need and suffers hardships in daily life is in great torment and necessity. Therefore whoever rescues such a soul from necessity acquires great joy for himself. For he who is vexed by such hardship is tortured with equal torment and torments himself like one who is in chains. For many, because of such calamities, when they cannot bear them, bring death upon themselves. Therefore whoever knows the calamity of such a person and does not rescue him commits a great sin and becomes guilty of his blood. Therefore do good works, all you who have received from the Lord, lest, while you delay doing them, the structure of the tower be completed. For because of you the work of its building has been interrupted. Unless therefore you hasten to do rightly, the tower will be completed, and you will be shut out.' But after he had spoken with me, he rose from the bed and, taking hold of the shepherd and the virgins, departed, saying to me that he would send that shepherd and the virgins back into my house.

Uses the brief's required English 'virgins' for the holy spirits who help keep the commandments.
Uses the brief's required English 'tower' for turris and keeps 'structure' for structura, preserving the building imagery of the Church.

pass_b_english: After I had written out this book, the angel who had handed me over to the Shepherd came to the house where I was. He sat down on the bed, and the Shepherd stood at his right hand.

Then the angel called me and said, “I handed you and your household over to this Shepherd, so that you could be protected by him.” “Yes, sir,” I said. “If, then, you want to be protected from every harm and every cruelty,” he said, “and to have success in every good work and word, and every virtue of righteousness, walk in his commandments, which I have given you. And you will be able to master all wickedness.

“For if you keep his commandments, every desire and sweetness of this world will be subject to you, and success will follow you in every good undertaking. Take his maturity and modesty into yourself. Tell everyone that he stands in great honor and dignity with the Lord, that he is a ruler of great power, and mighty in his office. To him alone, through the whole world, the power of repentance has been given. Does he seem powerful to you? Yet all of you despise his maturity and the respect he shows you.”
I said to him, “Sir, ask him yourself whether, since he has been in my house, I have done anything out of order to offend him.”

“I too know,” he said, “that you have done nothing out of order, and that you will not. That is why I say these things to you, so that you may persevere. For here, before me, he has thought well of you. But you are to tell these words to the others, so that those who have repented, or are going to repent, may think as you do. Then he may speak well of them here before me, and I before the Lord.”
“And I, sir,” I said, “declare the mighty works of the Lord to every person. And I hope that all who have sinned before, if they hear these things, will gladly repent and recover life.”

“Continue in this ministry, then,” he said, “and bring it to completion. All who carry out his commandments will have life, and great honor here with the Lord. But all who do not keep his commandments are fleeing from their own life, and they set themselves against him. They do not follow his commandments, but hand themselves over to death, and each one of them becomes guilty of his own blood. But I tell you to serve these commandments, and you will have a remedy for your sins.

“I have sent you these virgins to live with you, for I saw that they were kindly toward you. So you have them as helpers, to make you better able to keep his commandments. For these commandments cannot be kept without these virgins. I see that they are glad to be with you. Even so, I will instruct them not to leave your house at all.

“Only cleanse your house, for in a clean house they will gladly live. They are clean and chaste and hardworking, and all of them have favor with the Lord. So if they find your house pure, they will stay with you. But if the least defilement comes in, they will leave your house at once. For these virgins have no love at all for any defilement.”

I said to him, “Sir, I hope that I will please them, so that they will always be glad to live in my house. And just as he to whom you handed me over finds no fault with me, neither will they find fault with me.”
The angel said to the Shepherd, “I know that the servant of God wants to live. He will keep these commandments, and he will settle the virgins in purity.”

When he had said this, he handed me over to the Shepherd again. Then he called the virgins and said to them, “I see that you are glad to live in this man’s house. So I entrust him and his household to you, so that you will not leave his house at all.” The virgins heard these words gladly.

Then he said to me, “Bear yourself bravely in this ministry. Declare the mighty works of the Lord to every person, and you will have favor in this ministry. Whoever walks in these commandments will live and will be happy in his life. But whoever neglects them will not live and will be unhappy in his life.

“Tell all who are able to do right not to stop. It is useful for them to practice good works. And I say that every person ought to be rescued from hardship. For the one who is in want, and suffers hardship in his daily life, is in great torment and need.

“So whoever rescues such a soul from need wins great joy for himself. For the one who is harassed by hardship of this kind is tormented, and racks himself, with the same torment as a man in chains. Many, because of calamities like these, when they cannot bear them, bring death on themselves. So whoever knows of such a person’s calamity and does not rescue him commits a great sin and becomes guilty of his blood.

“Do good works, then, all of you who have received from the Lord, so that the structure of the tower is not finished while you delay to do them. For it is because of you that the work of its construction has been interrupted. So unless you make haste to do right, the tower will be finished, and you will be shut out.”
When he had finished speaking with me, he rose from the bed, took the Shepherd and the virgins, and went away. But he told me that he would send that Shepherd and the virgins back to my house.
notes: The section contains a Greek sentence embedded in the Latin text: 'καὶ ὥσπερ οὗτος, ᾧ παρέδωκάς με, οὐ μέμφεταί με, οὐδὲ αὗται μέμψονταί με' and 'λέγει τῷ ποιμένι: Οἶδα, ὅτι ὁ δοῦλος τοῦ θεοῦ θέλει ζῆν καὶ τηρήσει τὰς ἐντολὰς ταύτας καὶ τὰς παρθένους ἐν καθαρότητι καταστήσει.' These are glossed in the pass_a_gloss in their source order.
The Latin text uses 'hic pastor' ('this shepherd') where the Greek would have 'ὁ ποιμήν'; the gloss keeps 'this shepherd' to reflect the Latin wording.

problems.ruling: 'illum adversus' means 'against him' (the Shepherd), not 'against it' (their life). Wrong antecedent, misleading.

last_rejected.why: 'Adversus' here means 'opposed to, set against' (their own life), not 'turn against him'—wrong agency.
last_rejected.fix: set themselves against their own life
last_rejected.ruling: 'illum adversus' with 'fugiunt' means 'flee from him and against him'; 'turn against him' captures the sense adequately.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'in vincula est' means 'is being put into chains' or 'is imprisoned,' not 'like someone in chains.'
last_rejected.fix: as one who is being cast into chains
last_rejected.ruling: 'qui in vincula est' = 'one in chains/imprisoned'; 'like someone in chains' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: 'Adducunt' means 'lead on, induce, bring on'—they are driven to death, not actively bringing it; also misses passive suffering.
last_rejected.ruling: 'mortem sibi adducunt' = 'bring death upon themselves'; reflexive 'sibi' shows active agency. Rendering is accurate.

last_rejected.why: The Greek marks a shift to direct speech by the Angel (messenger), but English 'He said' obscures who speaks; should identify the messenger.
last_rejected.fix: The messenger said to the Shepherd
last_rejected.ruling: 'He said to the Shepherd' is clear in context; the messenger is the only speaker. No real ambiguity.

last_rejected.quote: I commend him and his household to you
last_rejected.source_quote: commendo eum vobis et domum eius
last_rejected.why: English omits 'to you' (vobis), weakening the reciprocal commending structure central to the passage.
last_rejected.fix: I commend him and his household to you
last_rejected.ruling: 'I commend him...to you' includes 'to you' in 'commend...to you'; 'vobis' is not omitted.

last_rejected.quote: the structure of the tower is not completed while you delay
last_rejected.why: Misreads purpose: 'ne...consummetur' means 'lest it be completed' (bad), not 'so that it is not completed'—the tower completing without them means they're excluded.
last_rejected.fix: lest the structure of the tower be completed while you delay
last_rejected.ruling: 'so that the structure...is not completed' correctly renders 'ne...consummetur' as negative purpose. No misreading.

last_rejected.quote: He told me that he would send
last_rejected.why: Latin 'dicens...remissurum se' is participial, simultaneous with departure: 'saying to me that he would send back'—English 'He told me' makes it a separate final action, flattening the dramatic exit.
last_rejected.fix: saying to me as he left that he would send back
last_rejected.ruling: 'He told me that he would send' adequately renders 'dicens...remissurum se'; participial nuance is stylistic, not a major error.
